## What the two tests answer

The spike-in test asks whether an unmixing setup returns a signal that was
added to known cells. It adds `k = cofactor * sinh(level)` times a dye's
spectrum to the raw detector values of chosen cells. Each setup then unmixes
the spiked files and the unspiked files. Recovery is the change in the dye's
unmixed channel of the same cell, divided by `k`. A cell "loses" the spike
when its recovery falls below `loss_cut`.

The score also checks an assumption of the method: unmixing is per cell, so
cells that were not spiked must not move. A file where any unspiked cell
moves by more than `baseline_tol` (arcsinh, any fluorescence channel) is
`coupled`; its recovery values are kept and marked.

The marker screen asks whether a setup squeezes a channel's negatives
towards zero compared with a reference setup. It flags a setup, population
and channel when the squeezed share rises in every donor and the donor
median rise is at least `min_delta`.

The package never runs unmixing for these tests. You unmix the files it
writes with your own setups (on a cluster, for AutoSpectral), then score.

## Mock example

This section runs on simulated data. Two mock setups unmix the same files:
`ols` is per-cell least squares; `clip` is the same with negative values set
to zero, which squeezes the negatives.

```{r}
#| label: mock-data
library(SpectraWeaveR)
set.seed(1)
det <- paste0("D", 1:6)
spectra <- rbind(
  A = c(1, 0.6, 0.2, 0.1, 0, 0),
  B = c(0, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 0.5, 0.2)
)
colnames(spectra) <- det

# Raw events: 300 per donor, abundances around 0 with noise.
raw <- lapply(c(d1 = 1, d2 = 2, d3 = 3), function(i) {
  ab <- matrix(rnorm(600, 0, 400), ncol = 2)
  x <- ab %*% spectra + matrix(rnorm(300 * 6, 0, 50), ncol = 6)
  cbind(Time = seq_len(300) + i / 10, x)
})

design <- sw_unmix_spike_build(
  raw = raw,
  populations = lapply(raw, \(x) list(T = 1:200)),
  spectra = spectra,
  dyes = c(markerA = "A"),
  levels = c(0, 1, 2),
  cofactor = 6000,
  spike_fraction = 0.5,
  seed = 42,
  key_cols = "Time",
  output_dir = NULL
)
design
```

```{r}
#| label: mock-unmix
# Two mock unmixers. Rows stay in raw order and keep the key column.
unmix_ols <- function(x) {
  coef <- x[, det] %*% t(spectra) %*% solve(spectra %*% t(spectra))
  colnames(coef) <- paste0(rownames(spectra), "-A")
  cbind(x[, "Time", drop = FALSE], coef)
}
unmix_clip <- function(x) {
  u <- unmix_ols(x)
  u[, -1] <- pmax(u[, -1], 0)
  u
}
unmixers <- list(ols = unmix_ols, clip = unmix_clip)
grid <- expand.grid(
  setup = names(unmixers),
  sample = names(raw),
  set = c("markerA", "base"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
grid$data <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
  x <- if (grid$set[i] == "base") raw[[grid$sample[i]]] else design$data$markerA[[grid$sample[i]]]
  unmixers[[grid$setup[i]]](x)
})
score <- sw_unmix_spike_score(design, grid, loss_cut = 0.5, baseline_tol = 0.05)
score
score$by_setup
```

The `ols` setup recovers every spike (recovery 1) and its unspiked cells do
not move. The `clip` setup changes recovery for cells whose unspiked value
was negative.

```{r}
#| label: mock-screen
base <- grid[grid$set == "base", ]
x <- lapply(split(base, base$setup), \(d) setNames(d$data, d$sample))
shape <- sw_unmix_negative_shape(
  x,
  reference = "ols",
  populations = lapply(raw, \(r) list(T = 1:200)),
  channels = c("A-A", "B-A"),
  cofactor = 6000,
  cut = 1,
  squeeze_frac = 0.5,
  min_negatives = 20,
  key_cols = "Time"
)
screen <- sw_unmix_marker_screen(shape, min_delta = 0.1, min_donors = 3)
screen$flags
```

## Diagnostics and report

`sw_unmix_diagnose()` turns both results into rows of the checks table. The
item is `setup|marker|pop`, the value is the donor median, and the reason
gives the number of donors and their range. **No limit is built in**: rows
stay `not_judged` until you pass one. The limit below is an example, not a
recommendation.

```{r}
#| label: mock-diagnose
res <- sw_unmix_result(spectra = spectra, run_id = "mock")
dx <- sw_unmix_diagnose(
  res,
  limits = list(max_share_lost = c(warn = 0.05, fail = 0.2)),
  spike = score,
  screen = screen
)
dx$checks[dx$checks$check_id %in% c("spike_recovery", "marker_screen"), ]
out <- sw_unmix_report(res, dx, path = file.path(tempdir(), "mock_report"), notes = "Mock data.")
basename(out)
```

The report adds the sections "Spike-in recovery" and "Marker screen" and
writes `spike_summary.csv`, `baseline_check.csv` and `marker_screen.csv`.

## Figures

F7 shows the share of cells losing the spike and each donor's median
recovery; F8 shows the cumulative distribution of per-cell recovery.

```{r}
#| label: mock-figures
#| eval: !expr has_fig
f7 <- sw_unmix_figure_spike_summary(score, readout_level = 1, stem = "spike-summary_markerA_T")
f8 <- sw_unmix_figure_spike_ecdf(score, readout_level = 1, stem = "spike-ecdf_markerA_T")
f7$plot
f8$plot
```

## Dashboards

`sw_unmix_dashboard()` reads run folders (a `report/` folder and a
`figures*/panels` folder) and writes one offline HTML file; a run with the
three CSVs gets a "Spike & screen" tab with the tables and the F7 and F8
images. `sw_unmix_dashboard_quarto()` writes a Quarto page with verdict
cards and one section per finding, each with Figures, Data and notes tabs.
Both write local files only.

`screen_bmv.R` in the source repository show the full real-data calls.
